One style object for every module of a document

Source: R/rtf_style.R
rtf_style.Rd

rtf_style() gathers the look of a document – font, size, row height, cell padding, markup, the header / footer colour – in one object, given to rtf_document() or rtf_config() as style = . It is an addition: every style argument of rtftable(), rtf_titles(), rtf_footnotes(), rtf_header() and rtf_footer() keeps working, and wins over the style. A study standard is written once, here; a report changes what it needs with the module's own argument.

Usage

rtf_style(
  font = NULL,
  font_size_half_points = NULL,
  row_height_twips = NULL,
  cell_padding_left_twips = NULL,
  cell_padding_right_twips = NULL,
  cell_padding_top_twips = NULL,
  cell_padding_bottom_twips = NULL,
  markup = NULL,
  color = NULL,
  title_format = NULL,
  footnote_format = NULL,
  title_width = NULL,
  footnote_width = NULL,
  table = NULL,
  titles = NULL,
  footnotes = NULL,
  header = NULL,
  footer = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

font

Font family for the text of every module, e.g. "Arial"; a named vector gives one family per script slot (see rtf_document()). A family not in the document's font_table is added to it.

font_size_half_points

The document's font size, in half-points (18 = 9 pt).

row_height_twips

The row height of every table-shaped element (content table, title / footnote, header / footer), in twips.

cell_padding_left_twips, cell_padding_right_twips, cell_padding_top_twips, cell_padding_bottom_twips

The cell padding of every table-shaped element, in twips.

markup

Cell-text markup: "script", "relational", "all" or "none" (see rtftable()).

color

Text colour, a 6-digit hex string such as "#7F7F7F". For now the shared colour reaches the page header and footer only.

title_format, footnote_format

How the title / footnote block is written: "text" (plain paragraphs) or "table" (a single-column table). The defaults are "text" for the title and "table" for the footnote. A border on a title or footnote needs the "table" form; the "text" form ignores it and warns.

title_width, footnote_width

The width of the title / footnote block: "content" (the table's), "page" (the writable width), a fraction in (0, 1] of the writable width, or twips (a whole number above 1).

table

A named list of rtftable()'s arguments for every content table: font, font_size_half_points, row_height_twips, row_height_exact, header_row_height_twips, blank_row_height_twips, the four cell_padding_*_twips, cell_valign, table_align, markup.

titles

A named list of rtf_titles()'s style arguments: font, font_size_half_points, row_height_twips, markup, align, border.

footnotes

A named list of rtf_footnotes()'s style arguments: font, font_size_half_points, row_height_twips, markup, align, border.

header, footer

A named list of rtf_header()'s / rtf_footer()'s style arguments: font, font_size_half_points, row_height_twips, markup, the four cell_padding_*_twips, border, color.

...

Not used: an argument not named above is an error.

Value

An rtf_style object for rtf_document(style = ) / rtf_config(style = ). Every argument left NULL is unset.

Details

The shared arguments reach every module that has the argument. A section (table, titles, footnotes, header, footer) is a named list that reaches its module only, under that module's own argument names; a section key beats the shared one. The order, highest first:

the module's own argument > the rtf_style() section > the rtf_style() shared level > the rtfreporter.* option > the resource baseline.

A section key reaches an element only where the element left the argument unset: NULL, or, for rtftable()'s table_align, cell_valign and row_height_exact and for a band's border, not passed. As for the module arguments, a font size and a row height resolve together: an element that sets its own size and no height takes no height from the style, its height following its size. A table is cut into pages (as_rtftables()) before the style reaches it, so a section's row height does not change where the pages break.

Row height, cell padding, vertical alignment and font size apply to the whole table (the body, and the header for its own settings); they are not set per row or per cell.

Several rtf_style() objects given through rtf_config() merge key by key, the later winning.

See also

rtf_document(), rtf_config(), rtftable(), rtf_header().

Examples

study <- rtf_style(
  font = "Arial", font_size_half_points = 18L,
  cell_padding_left_twips = 40L, cell_padding_right_twips = 40L,
  table     = list(header_row_height_twips = 260L, cell_valign = "center"),
  header    = list(color = "#7F7F7F"),
  footnotes = list(font_size_half_points = 16L)
)
study
#> <rtf_style>
#>   font = "Arial"; font_size_half_points = 18; cell_padding_left_twips =
#>     40; cell_padding_right_twips = 40
#>   table: header_row_height_twips = 260; cell_valign = "center"
#>   footnotes: font_size_half_points = 16
#>   header: color = "#7F7F7F"

adsl_tbl <- data.frame(Parameter = c("Age, Mean (SD)", "Sex: Female, n (%)"),
                       Placebo = c("75.2 (8.6)", "53 (61.6)"),
                       Active  = c("74.4 (7.9)", "50 (59.5)"))
doc <- rtf_document(style = study) |>
  rtf_tables(as_rtftables(adsl_tbl), titles = "Table 14.1.1") |>
  rtf_footnotes("Source: ADSL", font_size_half_points = 14L) |> # this report: 7 pt wins
  rtf_section(header = rtf_header(c(l = "Study XYZ", r = "Page {AUTO_PAGE}")))
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".rtf")
generate_rtfreport(doc, f)
unlink(f)

# A later style merges key by key over the document's:
doc <- rtf_config(doc, style = rtf_style(table = list(cell_valign = "top")))
